purpose: Freeze the long-lived inference-service TLS journeys used by the io_tls-v1 P1 gate before qualification.
common_setup_outside_measurement: one long-lived event runtime with one dedicated worker
one reusable TLS client context and one reusable TLS server context
one complete warmup episode per workload and route

common_semantics.provider: the same host OpenSSL build and default cipher selection
common_semantics.protocol: TLS 1.2 minimum with session caching and tickets disabled
common_semantics.identity: client verifies the same self-signed localhost identity and sends SNI localhost
common_semantics.progress: one external caller admits an episode to one dedicated event worker and waits for completion
common_semantics.completion: every admitted byte is checked and both endpoints exchange close_notify
common_semantics.failure: any connect, handshake, exact-transfer or shutdown failure invalidates the process

route_specific_implementation.hyle: public Scheduler, IoContext, spawn_task, TcpListener/TcpStream and typed TlsContext/TlsStream operations
route_specific_implementation.asio: public standalone Asio io_context, TCP accept/connect and async SSL stream operations
route_specific_implementation.interpretation: backend, handler/fiber representation and allocation counts are product-route outputs, not hidden adapters; the result can answer natural-route non-inferiority but not raw OpenSSL mechanism superiority

workloads.consumer: an inference HTTPS client/server connection establishment episode
a bounded inference streaming connection episode with repeated small records
charged_phases: 512 exact 256-byte client writes and server reads
512 exact 256-byte server writes and client reads

negative_space: raw blocking OpenSSL is diagnostic-only because it has a different progress and lifecycle contract
session resumption is a separate opt-in journey
certificate provisioning, HTTP framing, routing and model schema are not TLS-factor work
